summary.headline: Solar Industries Q4 FY26 revenue hit record INR3,053 crore (+41% YoY) with EBITDA INR870 crore at ~28.5% margin; FY27 revenue target INR14,000 crore.
summary.overview: Solar Industries reported record quarterly and annual sales of INR3,053 crore and INR9,838 crore, with Q4 EBITDA up 59% YoY to INR870 crore and PAT up 61% to INR556 crore. Defence revenue nearly doubled, reaching INR1,008 crore in Q4 (+134% YoY) and INR2,634 crore for FY26 (+94%). Management guided to INR14,000 crore revenue in FY27 while maintaining current EBITDA margins, backed by a INR21,300 crore order book. Working capital days rose above the 90-100 day range in Q4 on deliberate inventory build, which management expects to normalise over about two quarters.

financial_highlights.value: INR21,300 crore (c. INR18,000 crore defence, c. INR3,000 crore non-defence)

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,008 crore (+134% YoY) and FY26 INR2,634 crore (+94%). Management expects defence revenue to cross INR4,500 crore in FY27; the order book is about INR18,000 crore, mainly Pinaka-related.

segments.name: International / export
segments.commentary: Grew 32% YoY in FY26 to about INR3,800 crore. Share of basket was 33% in Q4 (from 36%) and 39% for FY26 (from 38%). Q4 international revenue was about INR1,000 crore, similar to the prior quarter. Management guides about 30% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Domestic mining (CIL, non-CIL, housing and infra)
segments.commentary: CIL share of basket fell to 9% (from 13%) for FY26. Non-CIL and institutional was 12% (from 15%) and housing and infra 12% (from 15%) for the year. Management says domestic mining demand was flat in FY26, with roughly 4% value growth, and expects a pick-up in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR14,000 crore while maintaining current EBITDA margins (around 27-28% for FY26).
Ex-defence revenue implied at about INR9,500 crore for FY27, with domestic and international growing about 30%: roughly 10-15% volume and 18-20% price.
Defence revenue expected to cross INR4,500 crore in FY27.
International growth expected at about 30% in FY27; long-run volume growth about 10% and value growth about 15%.
Planned FY27 capex of INR2,050 crore, after about INR2,700 crore invested over the last two years.
Dividend of INR11 per share proposed for FY26-27, up from INR10.
Working capital days expected to normalise over about the next two quarters once geopolitical uncertainty eases.
capex_capacity: FY27 planned capex of INR2,050 crore; management did not split it between defence and non-defence, saying the business is one and capex is prioritised by opportunity.
Recent expansion in Northern India through an acquisition; mega expansion in Western India just completed; new plants planned in East and South India, including Odisha and Telangana/Andhra Pradesh.

Africa: facilities in South Africa (hub), Zambia, Tanzania and Zimbabwe; Nigeria base with Ghana operational; Sierra Leone expected this year. Turkey base and Kazakhstan plant started. Small facilities in Thailand and Indonesia; Australia to start soon.
Medium-calibre ammunition facility commissioned and supplying samples for qualification.
155 mm: raw material intermediates already being supplied; coupling facility to complete the full round in the next couple of quarters, then 3-4 months before full-round supply begins.
demand_pricing: Domestic mining: FY26 OB removal was negative across Coal India, Singareni and private mines, yet domestic value grew about 4%; management expects FY27 pick-up as the shift to electric-based mining grows.
FY27 price contribution of 18-20% is expected from higher crude and gas prices feeding upstream and downstream products; volume growth expected at 10-15%.

Working capital build in Q4 was deliberate inventory stocking against geopolitical risk; management expects inventory gains in coming quarters and says rise-and-fall clauses cover only about 60% of commodity increases, with some contracts passing through after a quarter.
Ammonium nitrate price spike may cause a demand contraction for a couple of months; management does not expect an annual impact.
Management declined to give market share data for exports and dismissed concern over a possible Kalyani Group entry, saying it is not afraid of competition.

qa_highlights.question: Which new geographies are being targeted for international growth in FY27 (Zimbabwe and others)?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on Africa, with South Africa as hub and facilities in Zambia, Tanzania and Zimbabwe; Nigeria base with Ghana started; Sierra Leone expected this year. Turkey and Kazakhstan are also active, with Southeast Asia and Australia smaller.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Bhargavastra counter-drone system and 155 mm shell qualification?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhargavastra final-stage development; all trials expected in calendar 2026. 155 mm complete-round supply expected after the coupling facility is done in a couple of quarters plus 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports grow 2-3x in the medium term, and what investment is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue has grown from about INR800 crore (2018-21 plateau) to about INR3,800 crore now. Management would not give a multiple, but expects about 30% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the implied domestic growth (about 35%) for FY27 mainly low-base recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 growth of 30%+ across domestic and international combines 10-15% volume and 18-20% price, driven by commodity prices; mining demand expected to recover after a flat FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold given cost inflation and rising defence mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Price rises have been taken and rise-and-fall clauses exist, but a small margin impact is expected; higher defence and international mix should let margins be maintained at current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why were subsidiary earnings so low in FY26 (about INR50 crore), and what drove the working capital build?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence and international subsidiaries were subdued in H1 FY26 and improved from Q3, strong in Q4. Working capital days rose above the 90-100 range on inventory built to hedge geopolitical risk; normalisation expected in about two quarters.

risks_watch: Commodity price pass-through lag: rise-and-fall covers only about 60% of input increases, so Q1 FY27 margins could be squeezed before contract escalations catch up.
Working capital days elevated in Q4 on inventory build; watch normalisation over the next two quarters.
Defence execution: Bhargavastra and 155 mm timelines have slipped before, and the order book is concentrated in Pinaka-related orders.
West Asia freight and logistics headwinds; international revenue was flat sequentially at about INR1,000 crore.
Possible demand softness from high ammonium nitrate prices for a couple of months; possible competitive entry from Kalyani Group.
Subsidiary profit contribution was only about INR50 crore in FY26 despite the large revenue base; the improvement needs to continue.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, defence and FY27 targets, but guarded on specific product timelines and market share, which management said it avoids discussing. Management acknowledged a margin impact from commodity costs and an inventory-led working capital build.
